intro: Hi! In this lesson you'll learn the words you need to talk about your career and your education: applying for a job, your CV and the interview, your degree and campus life, and your skills and experience. Warm-up: what's your dream job, and what did you study (or what are you studying now)?
teachingNotes: Teach the words in three themed groups with an Indonesian gloss and practise them in short, natural sentences with Indonesian contexts (LinkedIn, job fair, fresh graduate, LPDP, UKT, SMK). Careers: apply for a job/position/scholarship, apply to a company/university, vacancy (US also job opening, poster 'We're hiring!'), CV (British) / résumé (American), cover letter (surat lamaran), job interview, hire, salary (monthly; wage = upah per hour or day), full-time / part-time, internship (magang) and intern (anak magang), get a promotion, resign / quit, resignation letter, lose your job. Education: primary school (US elementary school), junior high school (SMP), senior high school (SMA), vocational high school (SMK), bachelor's degree (S1), master's degree (S2), PhD (S3), major (US), scholarship (beasiswa), tuition fees (UKT, biaya kuliah), graduate (verb and noun), graduation (wisuda). Skills: work experience, skills (soft skills, technical skills), good at, fluent in, certificate, qualifications, qualified for. The learner already knows from a2-vocab-work-study: meeting, deadline, colleague, manager, work as a/an, subject, semester, lecturer, degree, thesis (skripsi), homework (uncountable), attach your CV: recap in a line, don't reteach.

Common error: *'I want to apply a job at a bank' (from 'melamar pekerjaan', no preposition). English needs FOR before the thing you want: apply for a job, a position, a scholarship, a visa. The place or organisation takes TO: apply to a company, apply to UI. Some American speakers now say 'apply to a job'; accept it if a learner writes it, but teach and test 'apply for a job', and never build a question where for and to compete.

Common error: *'I have many experiences in marketing'. When experience means knowledge and skill from work it is uncountable (like homework and work from A2): no a/an, no -s; say a lot of experience, two years of experience, work experience, How much experience do you have?. Countable 'an experience' is one event (Bali was a great experience), which is why 'many experiences' sounds like many adventures. skills IS countable (communication skills, two new skills). Common error: *'I'm good in English' (from 'pintar di/jago di'): good AT + noun (good at maths, good at Excel). 'good with people / numbers / computers' is also natural, so never test at against with. fluent IN a language (fasih berbahasa); 'speak fluent English' is also correct.

Indonesian traps: LULUS is two English words: pass an exam (lulus ujian) vs graduate from a school or university (lulus sekolah/kuliah; *'I passed from UI' and *'I graduated the exam' are wrong). Pronunciation: the verb graduate ends like 'eit' (GRAJ-u-eit), the noun a graduate ends like 'et' (GRAJ-u-et). S1/S2/S3 mean nothing abroad: say bachelor's/master's/PhD (D3 = a three-year diploma, only if asked). 'resign' is only a verb in English: Indonesian 'surat resign' is a resignation letter. 'fresh graduate' is common in Indonesian and Asian job ads; native speakers more often say 'recent graduate'. 'hard skills' is understood but job ads usually say 'technical skills'. kuliah = go to university / study at university (US: be in college); jurusan = major (US) or simply 'I study / studied law' (UK). British vs American: CV/résumé, primary/elementary school, university/college, tuition fees/tuition, vacancy/job opening, maths/math.

Limits: A0–A2 grammar only (present simple and continuous, past simple, present perfect with ever/never/just/already/yet, going to, will, can/could, should, have to, want to + verb). No passive: teach 'lose your job', and 'get fired' (dipecat) and 'get laid off' (kena PHK) only as phrases to remember; use 'get a promotion', not 'be promoted'. No present perfect with for/since (that's b1-present-perfect): say 'I worked there for two years' (finished) or 'I have two years of experience'. No second conditional, no relative clauses. 'good at + -ing' (good at writing) belongs to b1-gerunds-infinitives: accept it but keep examples to good at + noun. Don't teach CV writing or interview technique in depth: this is a vocabulary lesson.

keyPoints.title: Careers and applying for jobs
keyPoints.explanation: You apply for a job (not 'apply a job') and apply to a company. Find a vacancy (US: job opening), send your CV (US: résumé) with a cover letter, go to a job interview, and the company hires you. At work you talk about your salary, full-time or part-time work, an internship, getting a promotion, and resigning or quitting (the letter is a resignation letter). If a job ends badly, you lose your job: get fired and get laid off are phrases to remember.

id.title: Karier dan melamar pekerjaan
id.explanation: Kamu apply for a job (melamar pekerjaan, bukan 'apply a job') dan apply to sebuah perusahaan. Cari vacancy (lowongan; Amerika: job opening), kirim CV (Amerika: résumé) dengan cover letter (surat lamaran), datang ke job interview (wawancara kerja), lalu perusahaan hires you (menerimamu bekerja). Di tempat kerja kamu bicara tentang salary (gaji), kerja full-time atau part-time, internship (magang), get a promotion (naik jabatan), dan resign atau quit (suratnya: resignation letter). Kalau pekerjaan berakhir tidak baik, kamu lose your job: get fired (dipecat) dan get laid off (kena PHK) dihafalkan sebagai frasa.

keyPoints.title: School and university
keyPoints.explanation: SD is primary school (US: elementary school), SMP junior high school, SMA senior high school, SMK vocational high school. S1 is a bachelor's degree, S2 a master's degree, S3 a PhD. Your major (American) is your jurusan: I majored in law; British English says I studied law. A scholarship is beasiswa and tuition fees are biaya kuliah. Lulus has two English words: you pass an exam, and you graduate from a school or university. A graduate is a person who has finished university, and the ceremony is your graduation (wisuda).

examples.en: My brother has a bachelor's degree in accounting.
Sari got a scholarship, so she doesn't pay tuition fees.
examples.id: Sari dapat beasiswa, jadi dia tidak bayar biaya kuliah.

examples.en: I graduated from a vocational high school in Semarang.

id.title: Sekolah dan kuliah
id.explanation: SD adalah primary school (Amerika: elementary school), SMP junior high school, SMA senior high school, SMK vocational high school. S1 adalah bachelor's degree, S2 master's degree, S3 PhD. Jurusanmu disebut major (Amerika): I majored in law; bahasa Inggris British cukup bilang I studied law. Beasiswa = scholarship dan biaya kuliah = tuition fees. Lulus punya dua kata bahasa Inggris: pass an exam (lulus ujian) dan graduate from a school or university (lulus sekolah atau kuliah). A graduate adalah orang yang sudah lulus kuliah (lulusan), dan upacaranya disebut graduation (wisuda).

keyPoints.title: Skills and qualifications
keyPoints.explanation: Work experience is uncountable: say a lot of experience or two years of experience, never 'many experiences'. Skills can be counted: communication skills, computer skills. You are good at something (not 'good in'), fluent in a language, and a degree or a certificate can make you qualified for a job.

examples.en: Rina has a lot of experience in customer service.
examples.id: Rina punya banyak pengalaman di bidang layanan pelanggan.

examples.en: Pak Hasan is fluent in English and Arabic.
examples.id: Pak Hasan fasih berbahasa Inggris dan Arab.

examples.en: Dimas is good at design, and he has a certificate in UX.
examples.id: Dimas jago desain, dan dia punya sertifikat UX.

id.title: Kemampuan dan kualifikasi
id.explanation: Pengalaman kerja (experience) tidak dihitung satu per satu: bilang a lot of experience atau two years of experience, jangan pernah 'many experiences'. Skills bisa dihitung: communication skills, computer skills. Kamu good at sesuatu (jago, bukan 'good in'), fluent in sebuah bahasa (fasih), dan gelar atau certificate (sertifikat) bisa membuatmu qualified for a job (memenuhi syarat untuk pekerjaan itu).

blocks.text:
From A2 you can say your job (*I work as an accountant*) and attach your CV to an email. Now let's look for a new job.
- You find a **vacancy** (lowongan kerja, *loker*) on LinkedIn, on a company website or at a **job fair** (bursa kerja). Americans also say **job opening**, and posters often say **We're hiring!** (kami sedang merekrut).
- You **apply for** the job (melamar). You send your **CV** (British) or **résumé** (American, said 'REZ-oo-may'): the list of your education and work. With it goes a **cover letter** (surat lamaran): a short letter that says why you want the job.
- If they like your application, you get a **job interview** (wawancara kerja). If the interview goes well, the company **hires** you (merekrut, menerima kamu bekerja).

id.text:
Dari A2 kamu sudah bisa menyebut pekerjaanmu (*I work as an accountant*) dan melampirkan CV ke email. Sekarang ayo cari pekerjaan baru.
- Kamu menemukan **vacancy** (lowongan kerja, *loker*) di LinkedIn, di website perusahaan atau di **job fair** (bursa kerja). Orang Amerika juga bilang **job opening**, dan poster sering menulis **We're hiring!** (kami sedang merekrut).
- Kamu **apply for** pekerjaan itu (melamar). Kamu mengirim **CV** (British) atau **résumé** (Amerika, dibaca 'REZ-u-mei'): daftar pendidikan dan pengalaman kerjamu. Bersama CV ada **cover letter** (surat lamaran): surat pendek yang menjelaskan kenapa kamu menginginkan pekerjaan itu.
- Kalau mereka suka lamaranmu, kamu dapat **job interview** (wawancara kerja). Kalau wawancaranya lancar, perusahaan **hires** you (merekrut, menerimamu bekerja).

blocks.text:
**apply for, not 'apply a job'.** Indonesian *melamar pekerjaan* has no little word in the middle, so learners write 'I want to apply a job'. English needs **for** before the thing you want: **apply for a job, a position, a scholarship, a visa**. The company or university takes **to**: *apply to Tokopedia, apply to UI*.

**fresh graduate** (lulusan baru) is very common in Indonesian job ads. Native speakers understand it, but they usually say **recent graduate**.

id.text:
**apply for, bukan 'apply a job'.** *Melamar pekerjaan* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak punya kata kecil di tengahnya, jadi banyak yang menulis 'I want to apply a job'. Bahasa Inggris perlu **for** sebelum hal yang kamu inginkan: **apply for a job, a position, a scholarship, a visa** (melamar kerja, posisi, beasiswa, visa). Perusahaan atau kampusnya memakai **to**: *apply to Tokopedia, apply to UI*.

**fresh graduate** (lulusan baru) sangat umum di iklan lowongan di Indonesia. Penutur asli paham, tapi mereka biasanya bilang **recent graduate**.

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani is looking for a new job. She's sending her CV and a ___ letter to five companies.
blocks.explain: A cover letter (surat lamaran) goes with your CV when you apply. A resignation letter is for leaving a job, and there's no 'promotion letter' in an application.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Bu Ani is looking for a new job. She's sending her CV and a ___ letter to five companies.
id.explain: Cover letter (surat lamaran) dikirim bersama CV saat melamar. Resignation letter untuk keluar dari pekerjaan, dan tidak ada 'promotion letter' dalam lamaran kerja.

material.title: At work: from salary to resignation

blocks.text:
Words for your job once you have it:
- **salary**: the money you get every month (gaji). **wage** is upah, money per hour or per day.
- **full-time** (about 40 hours a week) or **part-time** (fewer hours, often for students).
- **internship**: magang. The person is an **intern** (anak magang). You **do an internship** (*an* because *internship* starts with a vowel sound).
- **get a promotion**: naik jabatan, a better job in the same company.
- **resign** (formal) or **quit** (relaxed): leave your job because you want to. The letter is a **resignation letter**.
- **lose your job**: the company ends your job. Two phrases to remember: **get fired** (dipecat, because of a problem with your work) and **get laid off** (kena PHK, because the company needs fewer people).

id.text:
Kata-kata untuk pekerjaanmu setelah kamu diterima:
- **salary**: uang yang kamu terima setiap bulan (gaji). **wage** adalah upah, uang per jam atau per hari.
- **full-time** (sekitar 40 jam seminggu) atau **part-time** (lebih sedikit jam, sering untuk mahasiswa).
- **internship**: magang. Orangnya disebut **intern** (anak magang). Kamu **do an internship** (*an* karena *internship* diawali bunyi vokal).
- **get a promotion**: naik jabatan, posisi yang lebih baik di perusahaan yang sama.
- **resign** (resmi) atau **quit** (santai): keluar dari pekerjaan karena kamu sendiri yang mau. Suratnya disebut **resignation letter**.
- **lose your job**: perusahaan mengakhiri pekerjaanmu. Dua frasa untuk dihafalkan: **get fired** (dipecat, karena ada masalah dengan kerjamu) dan **get laid off** (kena PHK, karena perusahaan butuh lebih sedikit orang).

rows.id: Gajinya Rp8.000.000 sebulan.

blocks.text:
**resign is only a verb.** Indonesians say *surat resign* or *saya ajukan resign*, using resign like a noun. In English: **I resigned** / **I'm going to resign** (verb), but **my resignation**, **a resignation letter** (noun). 'A resign letter' is wrong.

**get fired** and **get laid off** look like new grammar, but here just learn them as fixed phrases: *He got fired. Fifty workers got laid off.*

id.text:
**resign hanya kata kerja.** Orang Indonesia bilang *surat resign* atau *saya ajukan resign*, memakai resign seperti kata benda (nama benda). Dalam bahasa Inggris: **I resigned** / **I'm going to resign** (kata kerja), tapi **my resignation**, **a resignation letter** (kata benda). 'A resign letter' salah.

**get fired** dan **get laid off** terlihat seperti tata bahasa baru, tapi di sini hafalkan saja sebagai frasa tetap: *He got fired.* (Dia dipecat.) *Fifty workers got laid off.* (Lima puluh pekerja kena PHK.)

blocks.prompt: Pak Joko started as a sales assistant. Now the company has made him the sales manager. Complete: He got a ___.
blocks.explain: A better job in the same company is a promotion (naik jabatan): get a promotion. A vacancy is an empty job that a company wants to fill, and a resignation is when you leave.

id.prompt: Pak Joko awalnya sales assistant. Sekarang perusahaan menjadikannya sales manager. Lengkapi: He got a ___.
id.explain: Posisi yang lebih baik di perusahaan yang sama adalah promotion (naik jabatan): get a promotion. Vacancy adalah lowongan yang mau diisi perusahaan, dan resignation adalah saat kamu keluar.

id.title: Di tempat kerja: dari gaji sampai resign

blocks.text:
Foreigners don't know *SD, SMA* or *S1*, so say the English name:
- SD = **primary school** (American: **elementary school**)
- SMP = **junior high school**; SMA = **senior high school**; SMK = **vocational high school** (a school that teaches a job, like tourism or mechanics)
- S1 = a **bachelor's degree**; S2 = a **master's degree**; S3 = a **PhD** (said 'pi-eic-di')

At university: your jurusan is your **major** in American English (*My major is law. I majored in law.*); British English just says *I studied law*. A **scholarship** is beasiswa (like LPDP), and **tuition fees** are biaya kuliah (UKT; American: **tuition**). Recap from A2: skripsi is your **thesis**.

id.text:
Orang asing tidak tahu *SD, SMA* atau *S1*, jadi sebutkan nama bahasa Inggrisnya:
- SD = **primary school** (Amerika: **elementary school**)
- SMP = **junior high school**; SMA = **senior high school**; SMK = **vocational high school** (sekolah yang mengajarkan keahlian kerja, seperti pariwisata atau mesin)
- S1 = **bachelor's degree**; S2 = **master's degree**; S3 = **PhD** (dibaca 'pi-eic-di')

Di kampus: jurusanmu disebut **major** dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika (*My major is law. I majored in law.*); bahasa Inggris British cukup bilang *I studied law*. **Scholarship** adalah beasiswa (seperti LPDP), dan **tuition fees** adalah biaya kuliah (UKT; Amerika: **tuition**). Ingat dari A2: skripsi adalah **thesis**.

blocks.text:
**lulus = pass or graduate.** Indonesian uses one word, English uses two:
- **pass** an exam or a test (lulus ujian): *I passed the TOEFL test.*
- **graduate from** a school or university (lulus sekolah/kuliah: you finish it and get your certificate or degree): *She graduated from Unpad.*
So 'I passed from UI' and 'I graduated the exam' are both wrong.

**graduate** is also a noun: a person who has finished university (*a fresh graduate*). Say the verb 'GRAJ-u-eit' and the noun 'GRAJ-u-et'.

**kuliah** has no single English word: *I go to university* / *I'm at university* (American: *I'm in college*). Not 'I'm college'.

id.text:
**lulus = pass atau graduate.** Bahasa Indonesia memakai satu kata, bahasa Inggris dua:
- **pass** ujian atau tes (lulus ujian): *I passed the TOEFL test.*
- **graduate from** sekolah atau universitas (lulus sekolah/kuliah: kamu menyelesaikannya dan mendapat ijazah atau gelar): *She graduated from Unpad.*
Jadi 'I passed from UI' dan 'I graduated the exam' dua-duanya salah.

**graduate** juga kata benda: orang yang sudah lulus kuliah (*a fresh graduate*). Kata kerjanya dibaca 'GRAJ-u-eit', kata bendanya 'GRAJ-u-et'.

**kuliah** tidak punya satu kata bahasa Inggris: *I go to university* / *I'm at university* (Amerika: *I'm in college*). Bukan 'I'm college'.

blocks.prompt: American English. Complete: Dimas ___ economics at a university in Bandung.
blocks.explain: Your jurusan is your major, and the verb is major in + the subject: majored in economics (past, because he finished). 'major on' isn't English, and 'major at' has the wrong little word and the wrong time.

id.prompt: Bahasa Inggris Amerika. Lengkapi: Dimas ___ economics at a university in Bandung.
id.explain: Jurusanmu disebut major, dan kata kerjanya major in + bidangnya: majored in economics (bentuk lampau, karena dia sudah selesai). 'major on' bukan bahasa Inggris, dan 'major at' memakai kata depan yang salah dan bentuk waktu yang salah.

id.title: Sekolah dan kuliah dalam bahasa Inggris

blocks.text:
Job ads list the **requirements** (persyaratan) and your **qualifications** (kualifikasi: your degree, your certificates).
- **experience** (pengalaman kerja) is **uncountable** (a word we don't count one by one, like *homework* in A2): no *a*, no *-s*. Say **a lot of experience**, **two years of experience**, **work experience**, *How much experience do you have?*
- **skills** are countable: *computer skills, communication skills, two new skills*. **Soft skills** are people skills (teamwork, communication). Indonesian *hard skills* are usually **technical skills** in English job ads.
- **good at** something (jago, pintar): *good at design, good at numbers*.
- **fluent in** a language (fasih): *fluent in English*. You can also say *She speaks fluent English*.
- A **certificate** (sertifikat, said 'ser-TIF-i-ket') can make you **qualified for** a job (memenuhi syarat).

id.text:
Iklan lowongan mencantumkan **requirements** (persyaratan) dan **qualifications** (kualifikasi: gelar dan sertifikatmu).
- **experience** (pengalaman kerja) adalah **uncountable** (kata benda yang tidak dihitung satu per satu, seperti *homework* di A2): tanpa *a*, tanpa *-s*. Bilang **a lot of experience**, **two years of experience**, **work experience**, *How much experience do you have?*
- **skills** bisa dihitung: *computer skills, communication skills, two new skills*. **Soft skills** adalah kemampuan bergaul dan bekerja dengan orang (kerja sama, komunikasi). *Hard skills* versi Indonesia biasanya ditulis **technical skills** di iklan lowongan berbahasa Inggris.
- **good at** sesuatu (jago, pintar): *good at design, good at numbers*.
- **fluent in** sebuah bahasa (fasih): *fluent in English*. Bisa juga *She speaks fluent English*.
- **certificate** (sertifikat, dibaca 'ser-TIF-i-ket') bisa membuatmu **qualified for** sebuah pekerjaan (memenuhi syarat).

rows.en: Rina has a lot of experience in customer service.
rows.id: Rina punya banyak pengalaman di bidang layanan pelanggan.

rows.en: My year at a hotel in Bali was a great experience.
rows.id: Setahun di hotel di Bali adalah pengalaman yang hebat.

rows.en: You need good communication skills for this job.
rows.id: Kamu perlu kemampuan komunikasi yang baik untuk pekerjaan ini.

rows.en: Pak Hasan is fluent in English and Arabic.
rows.id: Pak Hasan fasih berbahasa Inggris dan Arab.

rows.en: With a TOEFL certificate, you're qualified for the position.
rows.id: Dengan sertifikat TOEFL, kamu memenuhi syarat untuk posisi itu.

blocks.text:
**Two traps from Indonesian:**
- *banyak pengalaman* → **a lot of experience**, not 'many experiences'. With an *-s*, *experiences* means separate events or adventures (*my experiences in Bali*), not your work knowledge.
- *jago di / pintar di* → **good at**, not 'good in'. (**good with** is also English, for people, numbers or machines: *She's good with customers.*)

id.text:
**Dua jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia:**
- *banyak pengalaman* → **a lot of experience**, bukan 'many experiences'. Dengan *-s*, *experiences* artinya kejadian atau petualangan terpisah (*my experiences in Bali*), bukan pengetahuan kerjamu.
- *jago di / pintar di* → **good at**, bukan 'good in'. (**good with** juga bahasa Inggris, untuk orang, angka atau mesin: *She's good with customers.* = Dia pandai melayani pelanggan.)

blocks.prompt: Interviewer: How much ___ do you have in marketing?
blocks.explain: Work experience is uncountable, so it has no -s and no an. How much goes with uncountable words: How much experience?

id.prompt: Lengkapi pertanyaan pewawancara: How much ___ do you have in marketing?
id.explain: Pengalaman kerja (experience) tidak dihitung satu per satu, jadi tanpa -s dan tanpa an. How much dipakai untuk kata yang tidak dihitung: How much experience?

resources.title: You're Hired
resources.note: A B1–B2 video series: a company hires a new sales director, from the applications and interviews to the job offer and the first day. Each episode has exercises and a transcript. British English, and a little above this lesson in places.

id.note: Serial video tingkat B1–B2: sebuah perusahaan merekrut sales director baru, dari lamaran dan wawancara sampai tawaran kerja dan hari pertama. Setiap episode punya latihan dan transkrip. Bahasa Inggris British, dan di beberapa bagian sedikit di atas level pelajaran ini.

resources.title: A professional profile
resources.note: A B1 writing lesson with a model LinkedIn-style profile (a summary and work experience), tips and exercises. Useful when you describe your own experience and skills.

id.note: Pelajaran menulis tingkat B1 dengan contoh profil ala LinkedIn (ringkasan dan pengalaman kerja), tips dan latihan. Berguna saat kamu mendeskripsikan pengalaman dan kemampuanmu sendiri.

pass an exam / graduate from university
a lot of work experience (not 'many experiences')

id.intro: Hai! Di pelajaran ini kamu belajar kosakata untuk membicarakan karier dan pendidikanmu: melamar pekerjaan, CV dan wawancara, gelar dan kehidupan kampus, serta kemampuan dan pengalamanmu. Pemanasan: apa pekerjaan impianmu, dan dulu kamu kuliah atau sekolah jurusan apa (atau sekarang sedang belajar apa)?
suggestedQuestions: Kapan pakai pass dan kapan pakai graduate?
Bagaimana menyebut S1 dan S2 dalam bahasa Inggris?
Kenapa tidak boleh menulis 'many experiences' di CV?

assessment.we-1: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Dimas applied a job at a bank in Surabaya last month.
assessment.we-2: Baca poster ini: "WE'RE HIRING! Barista at Kopi Kita, Bandung. 20 hours a week, evenings and weekends only. Great for students. Send your CV to jobs@kopikita.id." Pekerjaan ini full-time atau part-time? Jawab dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.we-3: Sari sudah tidak menikmati pekerjaannya, dan bulan depan dia akan mulai di perusahaan baru. Hari ini dia menulis surat resmi kepada atasannya untuk memberi tahu bahwa dia keluar. Lengkapi dengan satu kata bahasa Inggris: Sari is writing her ___ letter.
assessment.we-4: Lengkapi dengan satu kata kerja bentuk lampau: Pak Hasan ___ from Universitas Gadjah Mada in 2015 with a degree in law.
assessment.we-5: Bu Ani punya gelar S2 ekonomi dari Universitas Indonesia. Lengkapi dalam bahasa Inggris: Bu Ani has a ___ degree in economics.
assessment.we-6: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Budi has many experiences in sales.
assessment.we-7: Perbaiki kesalahannya: My sister is good in maths, so she wants to be an accountant.
